personality_one_liner: A calm, trustworthy, and clinical-editorial atmosphere that prioritizes clarity, human connection, and soft storytelling over dense data.

typography.handwritingFontFamilyNote: Caveat (Google Fonts, OFL-1.1), 600 SemiBold weight — chosen over Kalam (too heavy/casual for this editorial-journal tone) and Shadows Into Light (too thin/calligraphic to stay legible at small UI sizes) for decorative quote-callout text only, e.g. 'Progress over perfection ♡'. Never used for body copy or anything load-bearing.

spacing.rule: Use magazine-like spacing rhythms with generous vertical breathing room. Avoid dense card-heavy layouts.

do's: Avoid glassmorphism to keep the aesthetic purely editorial and matte.
dont's: No frosted headers or bottom sheets.

screens.name: Health HQ Dashboard
screens.purpose: A calm, holistic overview of the user's Food, Move, and Rest domains and their My Path progress trail.

states.loading: A soft, pulsing brand-colored circle in the center with a gentle 'Preparing your Health HQ...' message.
states.empty: No data yet. 'Your journey starts today' with an organic illustration and a CTA to log the first meal.
states.error: A calm 'We lost connection' message with a subtle retry button.

screens.layout: Top section: 'My Path' hero card with an abstract atmospheric sage background, showing the fixed-appearance milestone trail (no score, no human figure). Middle section: 'Food, Move & Rest' module with each domain shown separately — Food's strength components carry a direction-only Population Reference Marker (above/below/approximately-at national benchmark, never a raw HEI-2020 number), Move and Rest show logged minutes/hours. Bottom section: Cohort challenges and gamification (points/badges) displayed as minimalist list items. A floating action button (FAB) for meal logging and RAG LLM Chat Coach. Include a persistent illustrative-estimate disclaimer at the very bottom.

screens.name: Meal Logging
screens.purpose: A non-judgmental, process-focused meal entry flow via photo or text. (Voice logging was removed in 2026-09 — TAMU AI, the app's sole AI provider, has no audio/speech input to transcribe against.)

states.loading: Skeleton placeholders for camera and text input fields.
states.empty: A clean camera view or text prompt asking 'What did you eat today?' with soft lighting flatlay placeholder.
states.error: Message 'Unable to process the image.' with an option to try again or enter text manually. If no TAMU AI key is set, a calm inline prompt to add one in Settings instead of an error.

screens.layout: Full-screen camera view or text input with a soft gradient overlay at the bottom. Below the input, a confidence-gated review card that tracks process-based goals (fiber/sodium) rather than calories. Incorporate a 'Behavioral Safety Check-in' modal that appears if restrictive patterns are detected, using soft terracotta alerts.

screens.name: Curriculum & Games
screens.purpose: Scenario-based mini-games and video curriculum to apply nutrition information.

states.loading: Skeleton video thumbnails and game cards.
states.empty: No active courses. A serene message 'Ready to learn?' with a CTA to start the first module.
states.error: A calm 'Unable to load curriculum' message with a subtle retry button.

screens.layout: Editorial-style list layout. Full-width, borderless video cards with organic food flatlay background images, using a gradient scrim and white serif titles on top. Below the videos, the 3 mini-games (Plan Your Week, Menu Challenge, Build a Meal) are listed as soft cards with subtle icons. Generous vertical spacing between sections.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly adhere to the '3 Editorial Mobile LIGHT' personality. Keep radii small (6px) or 0px, and avoid heavy shadows. The UI must feel like a calming wellness journal.

Implement 'My Path' using the abstract atmospheric image provided as a single fixed-appearance milestone trail. NEVER show human weight or appearance, and never derive its position from a health outcome or an HEI-2020 score — only from logging behavior.
Ensure all prognostic outputs and AI RAG responses carry the persistent illustrative-estimate disclaimer in a legible but subtle typography style (e.g., small, muted color).
For meal logging, track the nine qualitative category tags (vegetables, fruit, whole grains, etc.) ONLY. Never mention calories, weight, or a raw HEI-2020 number.
Integrate a Behavioral Safety Layer. If restrictive patterns are detected, trigger a bottom sheet modal (using Gorhom) with a non-judgmental check-in.
All background images with text on top MUST use a vertical gradient scrim (transparent to surfaceInverse) to guarantee WCAG contrast.
Avoid glassmorphism for this specific editorial personality, keep surfaces flat, soft, and matte.
